explanation: Theoretical yield is the maximum product predicted by stoichiometry from the limiting reactant; actual yield is what you really recover in the lab. Percent yield = (actual / theoretical) x 100% measures efficiency and is normally below 100% because of side reactions, incomplete reactions, and losses during transfer and purification. A value above 100% signals an impure or wet product (or measurement error), not extra mass appearing. The animated beaker fills the actual amount against the dashed theoretical-max line while the gauge reports the live percent, mirroring AP lab and free-response questions.
bullets: Theoretical yield is the stoichiometric maximum from the limiting reactant.
Actual yield is the measured mass you recover in the lab.
% yield = actual/theoretical x 100; real reactions fall short of 100%.
Beaker level = actual; dashed line = theoretical max; gauge shows % live.
